claims.subject: root_buddhacarita
claims.summary: Agastya is named in an example used in a debate about desire.

claims.subject: root_udayin
claims.summary: Udāyin names Agastya while arguing with the prince.
claims.speaker: Udāyin
claims.note: A character’s retrospective example; not a meeting with Agastya.

claims.subject: root_udayin
claims.summary: The prince hears and answers Udāyin’s arguments.
claims.speaker: Udāyin and the prince
claims.note: This links the referring voice to its narrative audience, not the prince to Agastya personally.

claims.subject: buddhist
claims.summary: Udāyin’s example says Agastya desired Rohiṇī.
claims.speaker: Udāyin
claims.note: Narrative allegation in a rhetorical example, not independent biographical confirmation.

claims.subject: root_rohini
claims.summary: The verse identifies Rohiṇī as Soma’s wife.
claims.speaker: Udāyin

claims.subject: buddhist
claims.summary: The same verse also names Lopāmudrā.
claims.speaker: Udāyin
claims.note: The interpretation of the second half requires comparison of editions/translations; no new genealogical inference is imposed.

claims.subject: root_brihaddevata
claims.summary: A later explanatory narrative assigns the marital dialogue and student’s response.
claims.note: OCR translation checked; original printed scan and Sanskrit not collated.

claims.subject: lopamudra
claims.summary: Lopāmudrā is assigned the first two verses.
claims.speaker: Lopāmudrā, by Bṛhaddevatā attribution

claims.subject: vedic
claims.summary: Agastya is assigned the next two verses.
claims.speaker: Agastya, by Bṛhaddevatā attribution

claims.subject: root_student
claims.summary: The unnamed student is assigned the concluding verses.
claims.note: This student belongs to an explanatory tradition; no personal name is supplied.

claims.subject: vedic
claims.summary: The sage and his wife reassure their student.
claims.speaker: Agastya and Lopāmudrā
claims.note: Later reception of the hymn, not an extra verse of the Ṛgveda; unproofread OCR.
